prompt.context: Our client, GGC Health, operates eight Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASC) on the east coast. GGC Health has consistently been a profitable organization, but over the past two years, their ASCs' cumulative revenues have been flat at $400 million/year. The CEO of GGC Health is concerned about this and has hired your firm to increase revenues by 15%.
prompt.question: How would you recommend GGC Health increase its revenues by 15%?

clarifying_info.a: ASCs are modern health care facilities focused on providing same-day surgical care, including diagnostic and preventive procedures. They are seen as a more convenient alternative to hospital-based outpatient procedures.

clarifying_info.q: Who decides where surgeries are performed?
clarifying_info.a: Physicians generally dictate where the surgery is performed. They can perform surgeries at hospitals or ASCs.
No, pricing increases are not possible.

clarifying_info.q: How does GGC Health make money?
clarifying_info.a: ASC revenue equals the number of procedures performed in the facility multiplied by the expected reimbursement per procedure.

exhibits.title: Physician Group Membership by City
exhibits.shows: A stacked or grouped bar chart showing the percentage breakdown of physician specialties (Orthopedic, Neurology, Gastroenterology) across three target cities: Charlotte, Indianapolis, and Nashville.

exhibits.title: Average Reimbursement Rates Per Patient by Specialty
exhibits.shows: A table listing reimbursement rates per patient for six physician specialties.

framework: Increase revenue at existing 8 ASCs: grow number of patients per doctor, grow number of doctors per facility, optimize procedure/product mix toward higher-reimbursement specialties, expand types of patients (insurance mix)

Open new ASCs: analyze market attractiveness by city (physician supply, patient demographics, common ASC surgery demand), assess competition (existing ASCs, hospital strength), evaluate regulatory/reimbursement environment (fee-for-service vs. value-based care), identify partnership opportunities with physician groups or hospitals

questions.prompt: GGC Health has identified three potential expansion cities: Charlotte (30 doctors), Indianapolis (25 doctors), and Nashville (16 doctors). Using Exhibit 1, calculate the number of doctors per specialty per city. Which city can be immediately eliminated and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate multiplies total doctors by specialty percentages to get doctors per specialty per city. An excellent candidate quickly eliminates Nashville because Indianapolis dominates Nashville on every specialty (10 vs 8 ortho, 10 vs 4 neuro, 5 vs 4 gastro).

math.setup: Doctors per specialty = total doctors in city x specialty percentage
steps: Charlotte: Ortho = 30 x 0.80 = 24, Neuro = 30 x 0.10 = 3, Gastro = 30 x 0.10 = 3
Indianapolis: Ortho = 25 x 0.40 = 10, Neuro = 25 x 0.40 = 10, Gastro = 25 x 0.20 = 5
Nashville: Ortho = 16 x 0.50 = 8, Neuro = 16 x 0.25 = 4, Gastro = 16 x 0.25 = 4
Indianapolis beats Nashville on all three specialties, so Nashville is eliminated
math.answer: Nashville is eliminated. Remaining candidates are Charlotte and Indianapolis.

questions.prompt: Patients per doctor per month: Orthopedic = 15, Neurology = 10, Gastroenterology = 12. Using Exhibit 2 for reimbursement rates, calculate annual revenue for Charlotte and Indianapolis. Which city should GGC Health choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate calculates patients per year per doctor (monthly x 12), multiplies by reimbursement rate to get revenue per doctor per year, then multiplies by number of doctors per specialty per city to get city-level revenue. Indianapolis ($49.8M) beats Charlotte ($37.08M). Candidate should also flag that even Indianapolis alone does not hit the $60M target (15% of $400M).

math.setup: Revenue per doctor per year = (patients/month x 12) x reimbursement rate/patient; City revenue = revenue/doctor/year x doctors in specialty
steps: Charlotte Ortho: 24 x $900K = $21.6M; Neuro: 3 x $3M = $9M; Gastro: 3 x $2.16M = $6.48M; Total = $37.08M
Indianapolis Ortho: 10 x $900K = $9M; Neuro: 10 x $3M = $30M; Gastro: 5 x $2.16M = $10.8M; Total = $49.8M
Revenue gap vs. $60M target: $60M - $49.8M = $10.2M still needed
math.answer: Indianapolis at $49.8M is the better city, but it falls $10.2M short of the $60M target on its own.

questions.prompt: Since Indianapolis alone does not reach the $60M target, how could GGC Health increase revenues at its current 8 ASC locations to close the gap?
questions.guidance: This is a brainstorm question. Candidate should be structured and cover: (1) increasing patients per doctor — make ASC preferred environment, prioritize high-volume doctors, offer profit-sharing incentives; (2) increasing doctors per ASC — recruit new specialties, improve outreach; (3) optimizing product mix — prioritize high-reimbursement procedures, add new high-reimbursement surgery types; (4) patient mix — improve reimbursement by accepting patients with higher-paying insurance plans.

questions.prompt: GGC Health can add 2 urology doctors to all 8 current ASC sites. Each urologist brings in 8 patients per doctor per month. Using Exhibit 2, calculate the additional annual revenue from adding urology across existing sites.
questions.guidance: Candidate uses the urology reimbursement rate from Exhibit 2 ($8,000/patient). Total urologists = 8 sites x 2 = 16. Total patients/year = 16 x (8 x 12) = 1,536, rounded to 1,500. Revenue = 1,500 x $8,000 = $12M. Combined with Indianapolis ($49.8M), total new revenue = $61.8M, which exceeds the $60M target.

math.setup: Total urologists = 8 sites x 2; Annual patients = total urologists x patients/month x 12; Revenue = annual patients x reimbursement rate
steps: Annual patients: 16 x (8 x 12) = 16 x 96 = 1,536 → round to 1,500
Total incremental revenue: $49.8M (Indianapolis) + $12M (urology) = $61.8M, exceeding the $60M target
math.answer: $12M additional revenue from urology expansion. Combined with Indianapolis, total new revenue = $61.8M, meeting the 15% growth target.

brainstorming.prompt: How could GGC Health increase revenues at its current 8 ASC locations?

categories.name: Increase patients per doctor
ideas: Make ASC the preferred surgical venue by giving doctors more environmental control, better scheduling, and enhanced efficiency
Prioritize high-volume doctors in recruitment and scheduling
Offer doctors a higher profit share for hitting volume targets

categories.name: Increase number of doctors per ASC
ideas: Add new specialties (e.g., urology) not currently offered
Improve physician outreach and sales/marketing efforts to recruit additional physicians

categories.name: Optimize product/procedure mix
ideas: Prioritize high-reimbursement surgeries that generate more revenue per patient
Add new high-reimbursement surgery types to the ASC's service offering

categories.name: Optimize patient mix
ideas: Determine whether Medicaid/Medicare patients are accepted and assess reimbursement implications
Shift mix toward patients with higher-paying insurance plans to increase average reimbursement per procedure

recommendation: Open a new ASC in Indianapolis, generating approximately $49.8M in new annual revenue
Expand urology services across all 8 existing ASC sites by adding 2 urologists per site, generating approximately $12M in additional annual revenue
Together these two initiatives yield ~$61.8M in new revenue, exceeding the $60M (15%) growth target
risks: No costs were considered for opening a new facility or adding a new procedure — profitability must be verified
Indianapolis is not on the east coast, representing an unfamiliar market for management
Existing ASC capacity may be insufficient to accommodate new urology surgeries
Actual market share gains may fall short of projections
Physicians may not bring in the expected number of patients
next_steps: Conduct a full cost/benefit analysis for the Indianapolis ASC
If Indianapolis proves financially viable, begin site selection and construction planning
Begin recruiting and onboarding urologists at all 8 existing ASC sites immediately
Evaluate additional surgery types beyond urology for further same-site revenue growth
Assess feasibility of entering more than one new market in subsequent phases
